checklist.name: aortic tortuosity or elongation

quotes.text: Prominent features encompass aortic tortuosity
Tortuosity of the aorta was present in 21/21 (100%) patients
an elongated tortuous aorta projected laterally

checklist.why: The defining feature of ATS; present in every patient of the 21-patient series.

checklist.name: tortuosity of arteries other than the aorta

quotes.text: tortuosity observed in other arteries
tortuosity of other arteries was seen in 20/21 (95%) patients

checklist.why: Second defining vascular feature (pulmonary, head and neck and other arteries); kept apart from aortic tortuosity.

checklist.name: pulmonary artery stenosis

quotes.text: Pulmonary artery stenosis with an inverted V configuration of the pulmonary bifurcation can also be seen
stenosis of the pulmonary arteries (4/21 = 19%)

checklist.why: Named as a prominent cardiovascular feature and a main source of morbidity.

checklist.name: stenosis of the aorta or aortic branches

quotes.text: Focal Stenosis of Aorta and Aortic Branches
stenosis in ascending aorta (1/21 = 4%)

checklist.why: Focal systemic arterial narrowing is part of the classic vascular picture; separate from pulmonary stenosis.

checklist.name: aortic root aneurysm

quotes.text: (1) Aortic root aneurysm: echocardiography is recommended to measure the aortic root
aortic root aneurysm (2/21 = 9%)

checklist.why: Named prominent feature and the focus of echocardiographic surveillance.

checklist.name: arterial dissection

quotes.text: Aortic dissections, though predominantly seen in clinically diagnosed instances, can arise
Vascular dissection, distortion, and stenoses of the pulmonary artery branches

checklist.why: Serious vascular complication; the 21-patient series reports it explicitly as absent, so it is stated either way.

checklist.name: stroke or ischemic organ infarction

quotes.text: potentially leading to stroke and infarctions in abdominal organs
may cause a non-hemorrhagic stroke and infarctions in the abdominal arteries at any age

checklist.why: Ischemic events are a named cause of morbidity and mortality.

checklist.name: pulmonary hypertension

quotes.text: Pulmonary Artery Stenosis and Pulmonary Hypertension
These patients exhibited severe tortuosity, dilatation and stenosis of arteries, and pulmonary hypertension

checklist.why: Haemodynamic consequence named in the review's management table and in reported families.

checklist.name: ventricular hypertrophy

quotes.text: including severe ventricular hypertrophy, valvular regurgitation, and occasionally atrial fibrillation
left ventricular hypertrophy (1/21 = 4%)
mild left ventricular hypertrophy

checklist.why: Cardiac feature named by the review and found in both the case and the series.

checklist.name: systemic hypertension

quotes.text: Chronic hypertension and vascular stiffness are also common outcomes.
hypertension, which is a common concern in ATS

checklist.why: Called a common concern; blood pressure is checked at every visit.

checklist.name: hyperextensible or lax skin (cutis laxa)

quotes.text: cutis laxa (stretchable skin)
hyperextensible skin (n = 8)
The skin of the patient was hyperextensible (cutis laxa).

checklist.why: Core connective tissue feature, stated in all three sources.

checklist.name: joint hypermobility

quotes.text: Generalized connective tissue features include joint hypermobility
hypermobile joints (n = 8)

checklist.why: Core connective tissue feature.

checklist.name: joint contractures

quotes.text: hypermobile joints, and congenital contractures are distinctive physical manifestations
knee/elbow contractures
joint contractures (n = 1)

checklist.why: Called a distinctive manifestation; contrasts with hypermobility.

checklist.name: inguinal hernia

quotes.text: joint pain, cutis laxa (stretchable skin), inguinal hernia
Inguinal hernias were reported in eight patients

checklist.why: Common connective tissue feature and a frequent reason for surgery.

checklist.name: diaphragmatic or hiatal (sliding) hernia

quotes.text: (6) Diaphragmatic hernia/sliding hernia
diaphragmatic hernias were noted in seven patients
Hiatal hernias were found in five patients

checklist.why: Named for specific evaluation in the review; frequent in the series.

checklist.name: pectus excavatum or carinatum

quotes.text: pectus deformity
pectus excavatum (sunken chest) or pectus carinatum (protruding chest)
pectus excavatum (n = 3)

checklist.why: Skeletal connective tissue feature named in all three sources.

checklist.name: scoliosis or kyphoscoliosis

quotes.text: managing scoliosis, which is a common musculoskeletal concern in ATS
skeletal deformities like kyphoscoliosis
scoliosis (n = 2)

checklist.why: Called a common musculoskeletal concern.

checklist.name: arachnodactyly

quotes.text: pectus deformity, arachnodactyly, scoliosis
Skeletal features consist of arachnodactyly
long, thin fingers (n = 2)

checklist.why: Marfanoid skeletal feature named by the review and the case report.

checklist.name: down-slanting palpebral fissures

quotes.text: Typical facial characteristics associated with ATS include a long face, down-slanted palpebral fissures
with a down-slanting palpebral fissure
down-slanting palpebral fissures (n = 1)

checklist.why: One of the typical facial features, stated in all three sources; the only facial item, to keep the list from filling with dysmorphology.

checklist.name: respiratory distress or insufficiency

quotes.text: infants might require admission to neonatal intensive care units due to complications such as respiratory distress syndrome
five patients experienced respiratory distress syndrome
There is an increased risk for respiratory insufficiency

checklist.why: Respiratory complications in infancy; the series reports them in most patients.

left_out: aneurysms of other arteries, including intracranial aneurysms: rare; kept the list's aneurysm item to the aortic root, which the review names and surveils

keratoconus, keratoglobus, corneal thinning, refractive errors (myopia, astigmatism): named as evaluation and surveillance targets, rarely stated per patient in case reports; no ocular item fitted within 20
emphysema: named in the review's management table and as early-onset in one report, but rare
long face, micrognathia, high palate, convex nasal ridge, full cheeks: further facial features; one facial item kept to limit dysmorphology
cleft palate or bifid uvula: 'in some cases' only
umbilical hernia: less frequent (2/21 in the series)
valvular regurgitation, atrial fibrillation: occasional; 'occasionally atrial fibrillation'
autonomic dysfunction and orthostatic hypotension: named, but rarely tested in case reports
cardiac murmur or cyanosis: presenting signs rather than disease features
abnormal skin healing, pes planus, osteopenia, dental crowding, joint pain: management or surveillance items, less often stated per patient
muscular hypotonia: not in the main review; reported only in the series and the newborn case
diverticula (intestinal, bladder): only in the newborn paper's comparison table and the series
venous tortuosity, epilepsy, migraine: single reports

atopic features, nasolacrimal duct obstruction, cafe au lait spots, kidney malrotation and other features the series calls novel: the series itself says they may reflect consanguinity or be common in the population
atherosclerosis: described as a downstream consequence of tortuosity in general, not a per-patient finding of ATS
the GLUT10/SLC2A10 defect itself: present by definition
notes: The key review (Beyens 2018) has no open full text here, so under D-38 (as for Alexander disease and LAD-I) the checklist was written from three open sources only: PMID 37692180 (Ekhator et al. 2023, review; main source), PMID 39857743 (21-patient Qatari series, 2025) and PMID 36578839 (newborn case with literature review, 2022). Every feature is named by the main review 37692180 except 'respiratory distress or insufficiency', which 37692180 names only as a reason for neonatal intensive care admission; 39857743 and 36578839 support it. 39857743 supports 16 items with per-feature counts (all except arterial dissection, stroke or ischemic organ infarction, pulmonary hypertension and systemic hypertension; it reports dissection as 0/21). 36578839 supports 11: aortic tortuosity, dissection, stroke, pulmonary hypertension, ventricular hypertrophy, skin, contractures, pectus, arachnodactyly, palpebral fissures and respiratory insufficiency. Systemic hypertension rests on 37692180 alone. Some 37692180 quotes come from its management section and table, which list the manifestations to evaluate and treat. The 21-patient series carries one founder variant (p.Ser81Arg) and 71% consanguinity, and says its extra-cardiovascular data were not uniformly recorded; its 'novel' features were not used. No ocular item fitted within 20 (see left_out). Reference titles in the bibliographies were not used as evidence.
